mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and increased borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases are not followed by positive 60-day forward returns in more than 55% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals supply chain disruptions and reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines > 2% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 but the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST and RSAFS both increase but the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals disinflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate easing monetary policy.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL declines > 0.5% and the S&P 500 still produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and Industrial Production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1%, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and INDPRO declines > 1%
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and INDPRO declines > 1% but the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances, this hypothesis is rejected.
